title.value: Striking Into a Name: Percussive Naming, Grade Assignment and the Inheritance of a Rhythm on the Quiet Floor of Sounding

abstract.value: Names on the Quiet Floor are rhythms rather than words, and a name is held by one keeper at a time and struck into the dressed floor at assignment. We record twenty-six assignments and show that the grade of the floor a name may be struck into is fixed at the name's first use and thereafter descends with it, so that names carry economic rank independently of their holders. A former holder is addressed by a modified rhythm that is explicitly described as unfinished. Two names in our sample were struck into the wrong grade, and the resulting proceedings occupied the survey for most of a season.
